status: inferred suggestions, not recovered original answers; inactive until adopted
confidence_meaning: Confidence concerns correspondence with the existing wording, not certainty about the translator's original intent.

items.answer: Keep 6/8 while allowing variable phrase and stanza lengths to retain parallel clauses and repetition.
items.evidence: The setting labels its intro "6/8 throughout" and uses stanzas of different lengths, a repeated chorus, and a repeated outro.
items.rationale: The written setting supports flexible phrasing, but it does not record bar counts or prove a decision about additional metrical units.

items.answer: Use LORD for YHWH and God for Elohim and its inflected forms.
items.evidence: The lyric repeatedly uses "LORD"; verses 2 and 22 use "God".
items.rationale: The visible divine-name distinction matches this option.

items.answer: Keep "Of David" as a distinct introductory line, without interpreting the attribution as "By David" or "For David".
items.evidence: Verse 1 prints "Of David." separately; it is the first line of the arrangement's intro.
items.rationale: The wording and position are clear. Whether the line is spoken, sung, or only printed cannot be established from these records.

items.evidence: The lyric and arrangement have no Hebrew letter labels.
items.rationale: The absence of labels does not establish whether an explanatory acrostic note was intended or supplied elsewhere.

items.answer: Keep the transmitted clause order, with "My God" in verse 2 and both "See" openings in verses 18 and 19.
items.evidence: Verse 2 opens "My God"; verses 18 and 19 both begin "See".
items.rationale: These features favor retention over an acrostic reconstruction. An intention to add explanatory notes is not recoverable.

items.answer: Use a gender-inclusive singular such as ‘the one,’ with appropriate English pronouns.
items.evidence: Verse 12 has "the one" and "them"; verse 13 has "Their"; verse 22 has "all their troubles".
items.rationale: These are gender-inclusive singular and collective forms rather than representative "man/he/his".

items.answer: Use contextual verb time: perfect for established trust, present for habitual divine action, and future for expected guidance.
items.evidence: Verse 2: "I've trusted"; verses 8–9: "he teaches" and "He guides"; verse 12: "He'll show them". The arrangement uses "I've waited" where the lyric uses "I wait".
items.rationale: The result is mixed across verses and between lyric and arrangement, so neither offered policy alone describes every instance.

items.answer: Retain the report that the troubles of the heart have grown.
items.evidence: Verse 17: "The troubles in my heart have grown".
items.rationale: The first clause reports increasing trouble rather than asking for room.

items.answer: Describe God teaching the worshipper which way to choose.
items.evidence: Verse 12: "He'll show them which path to choose"; the arrangement says "He'll teach them which way to choose".
items.rationale: God instructs the worshipper in choosing, rather than explicitly choosing the way for them.

items.answer: Render sod as confidential counsel or a shared secret.
items.evidence: Verse 14: "The LORD confides in those / who fear him".
items.rationale: Confiding expresses confidential counsel rather than Greek strength/support wording.

items.answer: Retain the Hebrew virtues as personified guardians and omit the additional divine address.
items.evidence: Verse 21: "Let integrity and uprightness / guard me; / I wait for you."
items.rationale: The guardians are virtues, with no added divine address or upright companions.

items.answer: Make both halves declarations about who will and will not suffer shame.
items.evidence: Verse 3 says both "will be put to shame" and "None ... will be put to shame".
items.rationale: Both halves are declarations, not requests.

items.answer: State God’s habitual or expected guidance.
items.evidence: Verse 9: "He guides the humble in justice; / he teaches the humble his way."
items.rationale: The verse describes habitual guidance rather than asking for it.

items.answer: Use a direct request for pardon.
items.evidence: Verse 11: "forgive my guilt".
items.rationale: This is a direct request.

items.answer: Express a wish that integrity and uprightness guard the speaker.
items.evidence: Verse 21: "Let integrity and uprightness / guard me".
items.rationale: The guarding is a wish or petition, not a future assertion.

items.answer: Distinguish mercy/mercies from faithful love; retain faithful love in verses 6, 7, and 10. The setting keeps plural mercies and acts of faithful love in verse 6.
items.evidence: The lyric has "your mercy, / your faithful love"; the setting has "your mercies, / your acts of faithful love". Verses 7 and 10 retain "faithful love".
items.rationale: The distinction is clear, but the lyric and arrangement differ on plural/deed language, so no single offered option fully captures both.

items.answer: Use truth in both places.
items.evidence: Verses 5 and 10 both use "truth".
items.rationale: The same English term recurs.

items.topic: Soul, life, and the lifted self
items.answer: Retain soul throughout and preserve lifting language where English permits.
items.evidence: Verses 1, 13, and 20 use "soul"; verse 1 has "lift up" and verse 18 has "lift away all my sins".
items.rationale: The wording retains soul and makes the lifting language audible.

items.answer: Use wait consistently and retain the day-long duration.
items.evidence: The lyric uses "wait" in verses 3, 5, and 21, with "all day" in verse 5; the setting uses "waited" in verses 5 and 21.
items.rationale: Waiting, rather than hoping, is the recurring lexical choice; tense varies.

items.answer: Retain the recurring shame/be-shamed wording in verses 2, 3, and 20.
items.evidence: The lyric has "don't let me be shamed", "will be put to shame", and "don't let me be shamed".
items.rationale: The output preserves shame language. It does not establish a separate psychological theory of what shame means.

items.answer: Describe treachery committed without cause or justification.
items.evidence: Verse 3: "Those who betray without cause".
items.rationale: The qualifier explicitly describes causeless betrayal.

items.answer: Keep ways, paths, guiding, and teaching, allowing their meanings to develop through context.
items.evidence: Verses 4–5 and 8–12 retain "ways", "paths", "Guide", and "teach".
items.rationale: The road and instruction imagery remains visible.

items.answer: Use God my savior or describe God as the one who delivers me.
items.evidence: Verse 5: "You are the God who saves me".
items.rationale: The title is expressed as God's saving action rather than the abstract noun salvation.

items.answer: Use from of old or since ancient times.
items.evidence: The setting has "for they're from long ago"; the lyric has "through the ages".
items.rationale: The setting supports ancient time. The lyric alone is less specific about ancient history versus eternity.

items.answer: Repeat remember and do not remember, leaving their practical force implicit.
items.evidence: Verse 6: "remember"; verse 7: "Don't remember" and "remember me".
items.rationale: Remembering is repeated without substituting explanatory actions or adding good deeds.

items.answer: Preserve distinctions such as sins, transgressions or rebellions, and iniquity or guilt.
items.evidence: Verse 7 has "sins" and "the times I rebelled"; verse 11 has "guilt"; verse 18 has "sins".
items.rationale: The output distinguishes wrongdoing terms and does not use Greek ignorance language.

items.answer: Use humble.
items.evidence: Verse 9 repeats "the humble".
items.rationale: The lexical choice is explicit.

items.answer: Use in justice or in judgment, keeping the construction broad.
items.evidence: Verse 9: "He guides the humble in justice".
items.rationale: The broad "in justice" construction is retained.

items.answer: Retain covenant while rendering testimonies as decrees or requirements.
items.evidence: Verse 10: "his covenant / and his commands"; verse 14 retains "covenant".
items.rationale: Covenant remains, while commands explains the requirements rather than retaining testimonies.

items.answer: Describe people who keep or observe the covenant and its stipulations.
items.evidence: Verse 10: "those who keep his covenant".
items.rationale: The output says keep, not seek.

items.topic: The divine name as a reason
items.answer: Retain for your name’s sake.
items.evidence: Verse 11: "for the sake of your name".
items.rationale: The name image remains without an explicit reputation paraphrase.

items.topic: Because or although the guilt is great
items.answer: Present the greatness of the guilt as the urgent need for pardon, without adding "although".
items.evidence: Verse 11: "forgive my guilt; / there's so much to forgive".
items.rationale: The juxtaposition favors an appeal from need, but no explicit because/although connector settles the logical relation.

items.answer: Retain fear in both verses.
items.evidence: Verses 12 and 14 retain "fears" and "fear".
items.rationale: Fear remains explicit rather than being replaced with loyalty language.

items.answer: Keep the question and its answer-like continuation.
items.evidence: Verse 12: "Who is the one who fears the LORD?"
items.rationale: The question and following answer-like statement remain.

items.answer: Use broader language of dwelling at ease or in well-being.
items.evidence: Verse 13: "Their soul will rest at ease".
items.rationale: The wording expresses broad ease rather than explicit material prosperity. It cannot establish whether an afterlife interpretation was intended.

items.answer: Retain "seed" for descendants, but render the inheritance as "the land".
items.evidence: Verse 13: "their seed will inherit the land".
items.rationale: This combines features of different offered options; selecting any one option verbatim would misrepresent the outcome.

items.answer: Make God the implied subject who reveals the covenant to the worshippers.
items.evidence: Verse 14: "he makes his covenant known"; the setting has "he shows them his covenant".
items.rationale: God is the subject who reveals the covenant.

items.answer: Retain eyes, feet, net, and refuge without explanatory additions.
items.evidence: Verse 15 retains "My eyes", "my feet", and "the net"; verse 20 has "I've taken shelter in you".
items.rationale: The bodily and shelter images stand without an added explanation of enemy entrapment.

items.answer: Use alone, lonely, or desolate.
items.evidence: Verse 16: "I'm alone".
items.rationale: The output uses solitude rather than only-child wording.

items.answer: Use suffering language: pain, distress, and hardship, without making poverty or humiliation explicit.
items.evidence: Verse 16 has "in pain"; verse 17 has "distress"; verse 18 has "my pain and my hardship".
items.rationale: The actual equivalents express suffering; none of the offered phrasings exactly reproduces all these words.

items.answer: Keep the requests to see suffering and lift away sins side by side, without adding an explicit causal or transactional explanation.
items.evidence: Verse 18: "See my pain and my hardship; / lift away all my sins."
items.rationale: The clauses remain adjacent, with no explanation that suffering earns or causes forgiveness.

items.answer: Describe many enemies and cruel or violent hatred, retaining the emphatic repetition where meter permits.
items.evidence: Verse 19: "See my enemies—so many, / so violent in their hate."
items.rationale: The output describes number and violent hatred, not specifically multiplication and injustice.

items.answer: Leave integrity and uprightness unpossessed.
items.evidence: Verse 21 names "integrity and uprightness" with no possessive.
items.rationale: Neither the speaker nor God is explicitly identified as the virtues' possessor.

items.answer: Give verse 22 a separate stanza or typographical break while retaining it in full.
items.evidence: The setting gives verse 22 a separate "Outro" section and repeats that outro.
items.rationale: The arrangement visibly separates the communal conclusion while retaining its words.

items.answer: Use redeem and let the context define the requested release.
items.evidence: Verse 22: "God, redeem Israel".
items.rationale: Redeem is retained explicitly.

renderings.text:
Of David.

To you, LORD,
I lift up my soul.

My God, I've trusted in you;
don't let me be shamed.
Don't let my enemies
gloat over me.

None who wait for you
will be put to shame.
Those who betray without cause
will be put to shame.

LORD, show me your ways;
teach me your paths.

Don't remember the sins
of my younger days,
or the times I rebelled.
In your faithful love,
remember me, LORD,
because you are good.

He guides the humble in justice;
he teaches the humble his way.

All the paths of the LORD
are faithful love and truth
for those who keep his covenant
and his commands.

Who is the one who fears the LORD?
He'll show them which path to choose.

Their soul will rest at ease;
their seed will inherit the land.

Turn to me, show me mercy;
I'm alone and in pain.

The troubles in my heart have grown;
bring me out of my distress.

See my pain and my hardship;
lift away all my sins.

See my enemies—so many,
so violent in their hate.

God, redeem Israel
from all their troubles.

lines.text: My God, I've trusted in you;

lines.rationale: Combines all and not into none while retaining the opening emphasis.
lines.text: Yes, none who wait for you

lines.rationale: Moves the divine address before the petition for a recurring opening.

lines.text: for you're the God who saves me;
I've waited for you all day.

lines.rationale: Moves the divine address first to answer the chorus opening.
Fronts the emphatic you and brings LORD before the final goodness appeal.

lines.text: The LORD is good and upright;

lines.rationale: Adds to go to articulate the road image without supplying a destination.

lines.text: He guides the humble in justice;
he teaches the humble his way.
All the paths of the LORD
for those who keep his covenant

lines.rationale: Renders testimonies as commands, retaining their binding force while leaving their witness nuance unexpressed.
Moves LORD before the appeal to the divine name.
lines.text: LORD, for the sake of your name,

lines.rationale: Repeats forgive to express the magnitude of guilt as an amount needing forgiveness, with the causal connection implicit.

lines.text: Who is the one who fears the LORD?

lines.rationale: Recasts he chooses as the recipient's choice, resolving the Hebrew chooser ambiguity toward the instructed person.
lines.text: He'll teach them which way to choose.

lines.rationale: Combines lodging and well-being into restful ease, softening the lodging image and broader prosperity sense.
lines.text: Their soul will rest at ease;
their seed will inherit the land.

lines.rationale: Expresses confidential counsel as active confiding rather than a possessed relationship.
Folds continually toward into stay on while retaining the eyes.
lines.text: My eyes stay on the LORD;
Turn to me, show me mercy;

lines.rationale: Emphasizes suffering within affliction rather than its broader associations with deprivation.
lines.text: for I'm alone and in pain.

lines.rationale: Treats widening as growth of troubles and locates those troubles in the heart.
lines.text: The troubles in my heart have grown;

lines.rationale: Collects the plural distresses into singular distress.
lines.text: bring me out of my distress.

lines.rationale: Uses pain for affliction and hardship for toil or trouble, emphasizing experienced suffering.
lines.text: See my pain and my hardship;

lines.rationale: Folds the clause for they are many into a description, leaving its causal force implicit.
Compresses the hate-with-hatred construction and leaves its target me implicit in my enemies.

lines.text: Guard my soul and rescue me;
for I've taken shelter in you.

lines.rationale: Repeats the shared guarding predicate; guard expresses personal protection here, where the same root expresses covenant-keeping in verse 10.
Places God before the redemption request for direct opening address.
